name: Sorting Algorithms
description: Study of comparison-based and non-comparison sorting: quicksort, mergesort, heapsort, radix sort, and their complexity trade-offs.

observation.question: What does it mean to sort data?
observation.completionEvidence: Can define sorting and list common algorithms

principle.question: Why can't we sort faster than O(n log n)?
principle.completionEvidence: Can explain the comparison-based lower bound

application.question: Which sort for which situation?
application.completionEvidence: Can select sorting algorithm based on constraints

integration.question: How do sorting algorithms relate to divide-and-conquer?
integration.completionEvidence: Can connect sorting to broader algorithmic paradigms

creation.question: Can you invent a sorting algorithm for a novel constraint?
creation.completionEvidence: Can design custom sorting for special cases

isomorphisms.mappingDescription: Mergesort exemplifies the D&C paradigm from algebra
isomorphisms.limitations: Sorting has tighter lower bounds than general D&C problems

content.explanation: Sorting algorithms arrange elements in a specific order. Comparison-based sorts have a theoretical lower bound of O(n log n). Different algorithms optimize for different constraints: time, space, stability, and data distribution.
examples: Mergesort (O(n log n), stable, extra space)
Heapsort (O(n log n), in-place, not stable)
analogies: Like organizing a library: different methods for different collection sizes and constraints

memorized.evidence: Can name 3+ sorting algorithms and their Big-O

comprehended.evidence: Can explain how each sort works and why it has its complexity

applied.evidence: Can implement any comparison sort from scratch

analyzed.evidence: Can prove the O(n log n) lower bound and compare sort trade-offs

evaluated.evidence: Can evaluate which sort is optimal for a given data distribution

name: Quicksort
description: An efficient, in-place, comparison-based sorting algorithm using divide-and-conquer with a pivot element.

observation.question: What does quicksort do step by step?

principle.question: Why is quicksort efficient on average?
principle.completionEvidence: Can explain average-case analysis and pivot selection

application.question: When does quicksort perform poorly?
application.completionEvidence: Can identify and handle worst-case scenarios

integration.question: How does quicksort relate to other D&C algorithms?
integration.completionEvidence: Can connect to mergesort and general D&C

creation.question: Can you design a pivot strategy for a specific data distribution?

content.explanation: Quicksort selects a pivot element, partitions the array around it (elements less than pivot go left, greater go right), then recursively sorts the sub-arrays. Average case is O(n log n) with good pivot selection; worst case is O(n²) with poor pivots.
nonExamples: Merge sort (uses extra space, always O(n log n))
analogies: Like a tournament: pick a referee (pivot), split teams by who they can beat, then recursively sort each half

comprehended.evidence: Can explain why pivot choice matters and how partitioning works

applied.evidence: Can implement quicksort with different pivot strategies

analyzed.evidence: Can prove average-case complexity and analyze partition balance

evaluated.evidence: Can evaluate pivot strategies for different data distributions

transformed.evidence: Can design a novel partitioning scheme for a constrained environment

name: Mergesort
description: A stable, comparison-based sorting algorithm using divide-and-conquer with guaranteed O(n log n) performance.

observation.question: What does mergesort do step by step?

principle.question: Why is mergesort always O(n log n)?

application.question: When should you prefer mergesort over quicksort?
application.completionEvidence: Can identify stability and worst-case requirements

integration.question: How does mergesort connect to external sorting?
integration.completionEvidence: Can connect to external merge sort for large datasets

creation.question: Can you design a bottom-up mergesort for a linked list?
creation.completionEvidence: Can adapt mergesort to linked list constraints

isomorphisms.mappingDescription: Both are D&C sorts but differ in merge vs partition strategy
isomorphisms.limitations: Mergesort uses extra space; quicksort is in-place

content.explanation: Mergesort recursively divides the array in half until single elements remain, then merges sorted sub-arrays in order. It guarantees O(n log n) time but requires O(n) extra space. It is stable (preserves relative order of equal elements).
nonExamples: Quicksort (not stable, not guaranteed O(n log n))
Heapsort (O(n log n) but not stable)
analogies: Like a tournament bracket: split into halves, sort each half, then merge winners

comprehended.evidence: Can explain the merge step and why it's O(n)

applied.evidence: Can implement mergesort including the merge step

analyzed.evidence: Can prove O(n log n) and analyze space-time trade-offs

evaluated.evidence: Can evaluate when mergesort is optimal vs alternatives

transformed.evidence: Can design an in-place stable sort that improves on mergesort
